sections.content:
You know lo, la, los, las from Unit 12 and le, les from the last lesson. How to tell direct and indirect objects apart:
• Direct Object (DO): The thing, or the person the verb acts on (*Llamé a Carlos*). Question: ¿Qué? (What?). Pronouns: lo, la, los, las.
• Indirect Object (IO): The person who receives the thing (*Le di el libro*). It usually comes with a direct object. Pronouns: le, les (me, te, nos).

sections.title: Direct vs. Indirect Comparison
rows: Doy el libro a Carlos → Le doy el libro.

items.spanish: Compré flores y las llevé a casa.
items.english: I bought flowers and took them home.

items.spanish: Escribí a mi madre y le compré flores.
items.english: I wrote to my mother and bought her flowers.

items.spanish: A mi madre la llamé ayer y a mi padre le escribí.
items.english: I called my mother yesterday and wrote to my father.
